successors.name: Median Kingdom
successors.text: the Urartian lands, whose capital Van the Medes 'took over' in 590 BC (without the Euphrates strip round Kummuh and Melid, Assyrian-held since 743)

successors.name: Achaemenid Empire
successors.text: the Satrapy of Armenia that 'had replaced' the Kingdom of Van by the late 6th century

ledger.x: c. 860: the Nairi tribes are unified as the kingdom of Urartu under King Arame. 'The Nairi states and tribes became unified kingdom under King Arame of Urartu (c. 860–843 BC)'; infobox 'Established: 860 BC'. The page gives no extent; the region is the Van basin.
c. 832: Sarduri I founds a new dynasty. 'Sarduri I (c. 832–820 BC), the son of Lutipri, established a new dynasty' (the state, its colour and its dossier continue).
c. 832: the capital moves to Tushpa (Van). 'moved the capital to Tushpa (modern Van, Turkey, on the shore of Lake Van)'; infobox 'Tushpa (after 832 BC)'.
782: Argishti I takes the Ararat plain and the Sevan side.

c. 750: Sarduri II's Euphrates gains, Melid and Kummuh, are tribute-paying land. The Sarduri II page (reign 764-735) gives no year for the gain, only the 743 defeat; 750 is the year of the Cliopatria jump from 53,104 to 160,486 km2 and agrees with the Kummuh dossier's 'around 750'.

c. 750: the peak. The Urartu page names no conquered state for the east; the Sarduri II page has a campaign against Mannai 'whose population was exiled to Biaina'. The Menua, Argishti I and Sarduri II reigns (c. 810-735) together built the 160,486 km2 Cliopatria shape; the page gives no year for the Lake Urmia side…
743: Assyria strikes at Urartu's Euphrates bridgehead.
743: Urartu is pushed back across the Euphrates and loses Kummuh.
743: a single battle decides it; the page records no further fighting for the zone.
714: the campaign ends the same year; the page records no Assyrian annexation, and Cliopatria draws no change in the Urartu shape.

wars.name: Battle of Kummuh (Tiglath-Pileser III against Sarduri II's coalition)
wars.outcome: Assyrian victory: Sarduri II and his anti-Assyrian coalition were beaten 'somewhere in Kummuh' and Urartu was forced back across the Euphrates.

wars.name: Sargon II's campaign against Urartu
wars.outcome: Assyrian victory: Rusa I 'crushingly defeated' at Lake Urmia and the Musasir temple sacked; no annexation is stated, and Urartu recovered under Argishti II (714-685).

wars.name: Median conquest of Urartu
wars.outcome: The Medes, with the Scythians, overran Urartu and took its capital Van in 590 BC, ending its sovereignty.

certainty.note: Urartian borders are known from royal inscriptions and fortresses, not from lines; the page gives no treaty or survey frontier, so every edge stays soft.
